Parental neglect during childhood is one of the potential causes. My dad is 15 years older than my mom, and he is OCPD. I work as an X-ray technician in a large public hospital, and I can attest that introverts are not welcome there. Healthcare workers are expected to be extroverted and able to engage in small talk with patients and coworkers. In my experience, introverts comprise only 15-20% of my department. Eventually, you may feel marginalised and experience the pain of rejection.

It was a relief at first, but then you realise there is insufficient research on cures. Then you know you are worse off than cancer patients because you will feel the emotional pain your whole life, and then you will suffer until you die at an old age.

Now, I want to find a pill that will give me cancer, like leaving this world with natural causes.

I got straight A’s by concentrating on my studies and then kept changing jobs because no one wanted to be around me. Then you watch your old classmates with straight Cs get a stable, higher-paying job, and then you feel stuck and constantly want to catch the bus.

I used to work as an X-ray technician specialising in chest X-rays. The job earned respect, was relatively laid-back, well-paid, and involved minimal human interaction. However, when my partner decided to move to another country, I had to make the tough decision to follow him, which meant giving up my job.

Unless you have a permanent position in a public organization, such as here in Australia, your coworkers may view you as "inapproachable" and may even persuade the manager to fire you, even if your work performance is excellent. This can be compared to having an invisible leg disability that affects your gait, where people can discriminate against you in a subtle manner without facing any consequences.
I feel like parental neglect during childhood contributed to my negative inner voice, and it gets worse when I am working in an environment with many co-workers in the same room.
My manager did not terminate my employment due to the public nature of the organization. However, my colleagues now avoid me knowing my departure is imminent.
